newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada makes tobacco, MMT bills law.
newsitem.headline: Canada makes tobacco, MMT bills law.

text.p: Royal assent was granted on Friday to Canadian bills banning gas-additive MMT and restricting tobacco advertising and sponsorship, making the controverial measures law.

Just days before an expected election call on Sunday, 20 other bills were also given royal assent as the government rushed to squeeze through as much legislation as possible before dissolving Parliament for an election.
The royal assent ceremony also made law a bill for free trade with Chile, a Senate spokesperson said.

But two bills -- one to privatize Canada's ports and the St. Lawrence Seaway and another to make the labor code more flexible for unions -- will likely die, since they did not receive royal assent on Friday.

The ban on MMT has already prompted a US$250 million legal challenge. Ethyl Corp, Canada's provider of methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl, has launched a challenge charging the Canadian government with breaching its obligations under the North American Free Trade Agreement.
With royal assent given to the bill, the law may now prompt the government of Alberta to challenge the ban as well.
The anti-tobacco law will restrict tobacco advertising and ban vending machine sales of tobacco. The law will also restrict tobacco company sponsorship of sporting and cultural events.
Canada's tobacco companies have been trying to challenge the law in Quebec court.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent-owned by B.A.T Industries Plc of Britain.
The second biggest player, Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, is owned 60 percent by Rothmans Inc and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Rothmans Inc is a unit of Rothmans International Plc, which is owned by Swiss luxury goods holding company Cie Financiere Richmont AG.
Third place RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
